verdict.rationale: Glama's llms.txt claims every listed server is "scanned, scored" (glama-probe-1) and provides a browser-based inspector to test server capabilities before use (glama-docs-1, glama-docs-12, glama-docs-24), suggesting some vetting pipeline exists. However, the community evidence (glama-comm-1, glama-comm-2, glama-comm-3) shows the scoring system (TDQS) is framed around general quality metrics rather than explicit malicious/vulnerability detection, and reveals real operational friction (score not updating, undocumented paywall) that undercuts confidence in a robust, automated security-scanning pipeline. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of security/malicious-code scanning methodology, evidence of vulnerability detection specifically (not just quality scoring), and independent verification that the scan reliably catches malicious servers.
